app.name: Shopify (Admin API OAuth app via Partner / Dev Dashboard)

verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you have to register your own. Testing on your own development store works within the hour. You can also install on one real merchant store (or the stores in one Plus organization) with custom distribution and no review. Installing on stores from more than one organization means public distribution, which needs Shopify App Review even if the listing is unlisted. Shopify publishes no timeline; developers report 1-4 weeks, and protected customer data has its own separate review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to get to a working dev-store connection; 2-5 days to add compliance webhooks, a privacy policy, a listing and a screencast for public review
verdict.approval_wait: none for dev stores or a single custom-distribution store; 1-4 weeks reported for public App Store review

gates.name: Development store install
gates.unlocks: You create the app in the Dev Dashboard, install it on a development store under your partner account, and connect through Composio.
limits: An unpublished public app can only be installed on development stores under the same partner account
Unpublished apps with no installs on active stores have had their API access revoked; Shopify says to test on a development store
The API returns protected customer data from development stores only until the app is approved for it

gates.name: Custom distribution
gates.unlocks: Install on one real merchant store, or on all stores in one Shopify Plus organization, with no Shopify approval.
limits: One store, or all stores in a single Plus organization
Apps installed on stores in two or more organizations that were not submitted for review (or sunset) by Shopify's deadline have their API access revoked and are uninstalled
Protected customer data is not returned from non-development stores until the protected-data use is approved
Billing requires public distribution, so an app that charges merchants cannot stay on custom distribution

gates.name: Public distribution (App Store review, listed or unlisted)
gates.unlocks: Any number of merchant stores can install the app, from the App Store or from a direct link if the listing is unlisted.
limits: Unlisted only hides the listing. Review is still required before any merchant can install
From January 1, 2027, public apps must use expiring offline access tokens (60 minutes, rotated automatically)
Scopes marked 'Shopify approval required' (e.g. read_all_orders) need separate approval before you can declare them
Level 2 protected customer data (name, address, email, phone) reportedly needs a data protection review
gates.time_to_reach: 1-4 weeks reported per review cycle; re-reviews reportedly move faster

steps.title: Create a Shopify Partner account
steps.detail: Go to the Shopify Partners page and click 'Become a partner'. Sign up with your business identity. A third-party blog mentions a one-time $19 registration fee before you can list apps; check Shopify's own partner pages before relying on that.

steps.title: Create a development store
steps.detail: From your partner account, create a development store to test on. Before review, a public app can only be installed on development stores under the same partner account. Shopify also tells developers testing unpublished apps to use a development store.
gotchas: Protected customer data is returned only from development stores until your app is approved for it.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Dev Dashboard. Since January 1, 2026, new custom apps can no longer be created in the Shopify admin. Copy the app's client ID and client secret for Composio.
gotchas: Don't put 'Shopify' in the app name. Community reports list it as a common rejection reason.

steps.title: Register the allowed redirection URL
steps.detail: In the app's Dev Dashboard configuration, add the full callback URL to the allowed redirection URLs. Shopify requires the complete redirect_uri sent in the grant request to be on this list. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Wildcard and partial matching rules are not documented in the findings. Register the exact URL.

steps.title: Pick the minimum set of scopes
steps.detail: Composio's default list asks for read/write pairs on many resources. Cut it down to what your agent actually uses. Shopify reportedly removes unnecessary scopes during review, and excess scopes are a common rejection reason. Keep 'Shopify approval required' scopes such as read_all_orders out unless you need them.

steps.title: Create a custom OAuth auth config in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Shopify auth config with your own client ID, client secret and the reduced scope list. Composio builds the authorize URL on the merchant's shop domain (https://{shop}/admin/oauth/authorize, with client_id, scope, redirect_uri and state).

steps.title: Run a test authorization against your development store
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection using your development store's myshopify.com subdomain. Approve the grant screen, then confirm an Admin API call works.
gotchas: The grant screen can't load inside the Shopify admin iframe (X-Frame-Options: DENY). Embedded apps must break out of the iframe first.
For review, the app must send merchants to its UI after they accept permissions.

steps.title: Optional: use custom distribution for a single merchant
steps.detail: If only one store (or the stores in one Plus organization) needs the app, choose custom distribution and install it there. No review is needed. Once you need stores in two or more organizations, submit for public review, or Shopify will revoke API access by its deadline.

steps.title: Implement the mandatory compliance webhooks and publish a privacy policy
steps.detail: Subscribe to Shopify's mandatory compliance (GDPR) webhooks and make sure the endpoints respond. Draft a privacy policy that mentions Shopify and the data the app touches. Host it at a public URL with no login.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access if you need it
steps.detail: Protected customer data is off by default and reviewed separately from scope approval. After you select a distribution method, request it under API access requests in the Partner Dashboard and fill in the data-protection details. Expect questions about access logging, staff access controls, encryption and incident response.

steps.title: Support expiring offline access tokens
steps.detail: From January 1, 2027, public apps must use expiring offline access tokens (60 minutes, rotated automatically) for the Admin API. Existing tokens can be exchanged in code without merchants reinstalling. Confirm that your Composio connection handles token rotation.

steps.title: Prepare the listing, test instructions and screencast
steps.detail: Fill in the app name, description, screenshots, support URL and privacy policy URL. Write clear test instructions and record a full screencast of setup and functionality. If the app charges merchants, it must use Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API.

steps.title: Submit for App Review and wait
steps.detail: Submit the app. Shopify publishes no timeline. Developers report 1-2 weeks per cycle and up to 3-4 weeks before a reviewer is assigned. Fix any feedback and resubmit; re-reviews reportedly go faster.

requirements.detail: Needed to create apps and development stores. A one-time $19 fee is reported by a third party only.

requirements.item: App created in the Dev Dashboard
requirements.detail: New custom apps can't be created in the Shopify admin since January 1, 2026.
The complete redirect_uri must be listed as an allowed redirection URL.

requirements.item: Custom distribution limited to one store or one Plus organization
requirements.detail: No approval needed, but installing across more than one organization requires public review.

requirements.item: Privacy policy at a public URL
requirements.detail: Must be linked from the App Store listing and reachable without login.
Required for public apps. Missing or broken endpoints are a commonly reported rejection reason.

requirements.item: Shopify Billing API / App Pricing for any charges
requirements.detail: All app charges must go through Shopify.
A complete screencast of setup and functionality, plus clear test instructions.
Required for all public apps from January 1, 2027. Custom apps are exempt.
Separate from scope approval. Without it, no protected data is returned from non-development stores.

scopes.scope: read_products / write_products, read_orders / write_orders, read_inventory, read_fulfillments, etc.
scopes.effect: You can declare these freely, but review checks that each one is necessary. Drop the ones you don't use from Composio's long default list.
Shopify must approve the app before you can declare this scope. Without it, only orders from the default 60-day window are visible.

scopes.scope: read_apps, subscription scopes and other 'Shopify approval required' scopes
scopes.effect: Need Shopify approval before you can declare them. For other labeled scopes, contact Shopify Support and explain why you need them.

You can declare them, but non-development stores return no protected data until the protected customer data request is approved. Level 2 fields (name, address, email, phone) reportedly need a data protection review.

blockers.symptom: Merchants can't install your unlisted app before review
blockers.cause: Unlisted apps are still public apps. Unlisted only hides the listing; review is still required.
blockers.fix: Submit for App Review, or use custom distribution if only one store or one Plus organization needs the app.

blockers.symptom: 'This app is under review' banner blocks installation, even from the Dev Dashboard
blockers.cause: Public distribution with billing is configured and review is pending. Billing requires public distribution.
blockers.fix: Test on development stores under your partner account until review passes, or leave billing out of the build you test on external stores.

blockers.symptom: API access revoked or app uninstalled from merchant stores
blockers.cause: The unpublished app was installed on stores in two or more organizations and wasn't submitted for review by Shopify's deadline, or it had no installs on active stores.
blockers.fix: Submit the app for review, or keep it to custom distribution on a single store or Plus organization. Test on development stores.

blockers.symptom: Customer fields come back empty on real stores
blockers.cause: Protected customer data isn't approved yet. It is reviewed separately from scope approval.
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data access in the Partner Dashboard and complete the data-protection details.

blockers.cause: Commonly reported reasons: missing or broken GDPR webhooks, unnecessary scopes, 'Shopify' in the app name, a broken OAuth/install flow, or no redirect to the app UI after the grant.
blockers.fix: Fix the listed issues and resubmit. Re-reviews reportedly go faster.

blockers.symptom: OAuth grant screen won't load inside the Shopify admin
blockers.cause: The grant screen sends X-Frame-Options: DENY.
blockers.fix: Break out of the iframe with an App Bridge redirect before sending the user to the grant screen.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you always need your own. Create the app in Shopify's Dev Dashboard, register the Composio callback URL as an allowed redirection URL, and enter the client ID and secret as a custom OAuth auth config. Composio's default scope list is long; keep only what your agent uses, since Shopify reviews scope necessity. A development store or a single custom-distribution store needs no review. Merchants across more than one organization need App Store review.

open_questions: Does Composio's Shopify integration handle expiring offline tokens (refresh and rotation) once they are required on January 1, 2027? The refresh-token call and its expiry were not checked in an official doc.
Is PKCE supported in Shopify's authorization-code flow? Not confirmed.
Is there a numeric install cap for unreviewed public apps? None was found.
Review timeline: Shopify publishes none. Community reports range from about 1 to 4 weeks.
The $19 partner registration fee comes only from a third-party blog.
Redirect URL matching and wildcard rules were not verified beyond 'the complete URL must be added'.
Protected customer data levels and review steps rely on community summaries; the official protected-data page could not be fetched.
The app review checklist and best-practices pages were only seen in search excerpts.
